title: Post Office

vibeProfile.oneLine: Bukowski's boozing alter ego survives years of soul-killing postal work.

summary: Henry Chinaski, Bukowski's boozing, gambling, women-chasing alter ego, drags himself through years of soul-killing work at the US Postal Service in this, Bukowski's first novel. Told in short, flat, funny bursts, it is a bruised comedy about dead-end jobs, hangovers and survival at the bottom of American life. Crude, direct and weirdly life-affirming, it launched the Chinaski saga and Bukowski's reputation as the poet laureate of the down and out.
whyReadIt: Bukowski's raw, funny debut about hating your job and drinking through it. Crude, direct and oddly life-affirming.

funFacts.text: Bukowski really did work at the post office for years before quitting to write full-time at fifty.
